column4: oa-kirchberg: Kirchberg's Theorem 1.1 is proved with no input, at the trace side of the factorization property (the repository definition, Ozawa's (F)), along a real dilation of the models, the completed tensor square, the Kazhdan near-invariant vector, compact extraction and Mal'cev. Open: the Corollary 1.2 clause, "every subgroup of the unitary group of R has the factorization property".

oa-kirchberg: "So G does not have the factorization property", for every infinite simple Kazhdan group, from Theorem 1.1 and not_isResiduallyFinite_of_isSimpleGroup_of_infinite. Open: "it is not a subgroup of the unitary group of R" (needs Corollary 1.2); the LLP clause belongs to oa-llp.

oa-kirchberg: Thom's construction (a finitely generated Kazhdan LEF group that is not residually finite, and not simple) is cited credit that no later step of the note uses. It remains the typed input ThomSoficKazhdanNonResiduallyFiniteInput and is not proved. The asserted inference "not residually finite and so lacks the factorization property" is carried for every Kazhdan group by the closed endpoint printedKazhdanNotResiduallyFiniteLacksFactorizationProperty, the contrapositive of Kirchberg's Theorem 1.1. Text verified at f34e9c0b1 l.93-95.

oa-kirchberg: abstract l.30-33 at 8b36733d7. printedSimpleKazhdanSoficMain at n = 3: for every infinite minimal subshift over a finite alphabet, G_X is infinite, finitely generated, simple and Kazhdan, and PrintedMarkedLimitExpanders gives the marked limit of the simple groups SL_{3N}(F_2) whose Cayley graphs form an expander family.

oa-kirchberg: abstract l.33-36. LEF, sofic and hyperlinear are the last three clauses of printedSimpleKazhdanSoficMain. The answer along the printed route through G_X is the closed printedGXAnswersBrownOzawaPestov (17af31bea): for the Toeplitz subshift X, G_X is infinite, simple, Kazhdan, sofic and hyperlinear. The names of Brown, Ozawa and Pestov are credit. Re-cited after oa-expanders' audit: the earlier carrier was the conditional _of_main, and the Pestov91 answer is a different group.

oa-kirchberg: l.73-75. IsTextbookLEF is the printed definition verbatim: every finite subset maps injectively into a finite group, preserving the products that stay in the subset. The project convention IsLEF (permutation targets, all pairwise products) is equivalent by the proved isLEF_iff_textbook. The citation of Vershik and Gordon is credit.

oa-kirchberg: l.75-77. printedSubshiftRingFGStatement: LC(X,F_2) ⋊_T Z is a finitely generated ring. printedEJZTheorem: EL_n of a finitely generated ring has property (T), proved in the repository with no input. The (T) clause of printedSimpleKazhdanSoficMain combines them. The citations of Ershov–Jaikin-Zapirain and Kazhdan are credit.

oa-kirchberg: l.77-80. printedPeriodicMatricialStatement: periodic approximations give maps phi_k : R -> M_{N_k}(F_2), unital, generating and eventually additive and multiplicative (IsMatricialVia). printedFiniteModelsRing: the finite models from periodic words. The comparison with Grigorchuk and Medynets' proof is credit.

oa-kirchberg: l.80-82. The marked limit of SL_{3N}(F_2) with an expander family is the PrintedMarkedLimitExpanders clause of printedSimpleKazhdanSoficMain, through printedMatricialMarkedLimitStatement and printedMatricialQuotientsExpanders. "as in Kassabov's construction" is credit.

oa-kirchberg: l.82-85, the simplicity route. General.isSimpleGroup_clopenGroupCrossedProduct combines two steps. First, the commutator witness (GeneralCommutatorSpan, GeneralTowerCopy): a nontrivial normal subgroup contains a nontrivial commutator in the copy H_V of GL_d(F_2) over a clopen tower. Second, isSimpleGroup_of_generalCommutatorWitness: K ∩ H_V is normal in the simple group GL_d(F_2) = PSL_d(F_2), so K contains H_V and an elementary matrix, hence K = G. printedGeneralSimplicityStatement carries it at the printed hypotheses, and printedSimpleKazhdanSoficMain specializes it to G_X.
oa-kirchberg: l.85-88. Matui's similar argument for derived topological full groups is cited credit, and no step of the note uses it.
